thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — PrivateLink / customer VPNs in us-west3 reporting intermittent connectivity. Multiple BGP session resets seen in the last 3m. AUTO-PRIO: page oncall. :rotating_light:

pagerduty-oncall: grabbing it. what's the customer impact?

Carla (SRE): seeing route withdraws from peer ASN 64501 across two PrivateLink endpoints in us-west3-a/b. Some customers losing reachability to private endpoints, others seeing asymmetric paths.

Mike (NetOps): I can confirm. BGP logs show repeated TCP retrans and session flaps. Looks like an ECMP asymmetric path collapse between our edge and provider PoP.

Raj (Eng-Platform): tagging infra and netops. any signs of control plane storms on our side?

Lucas (Infra): control plane looks healthy for host agents. No spikes in CPU/mem on edge routers. Links show occasional packet loss on interface eth0/3 to transit-1.

Carla (SRE): quick impact assessment: 6 customers with private connectivity degraded; 2 in active failover; 4 reporting intermittent DNS failures for private hostnames behind PrivateLink. No data plane CPU spikes.

Tina (Customer Success): I've reached out to the top impacted customer (FinSaaS). They're seeing timeouts to private API endpoints. They want ETA and mitigation steps.

Mike (NetOps): running targeted checks now. dump from edge router near us-west3-a:
```
show bgp neighbors 203.0.113.5
Neighbor is 203.0.113.5, remote AS 64501, 4 established, 3 connects in last 5m
  Last reset 00:00:30, 10 resets in 3m
  Prefixes received 128, accepted 128
```

Carla (SRE): digging DNS side for PrivateLink DNS forwarding. Running dig toward internal resolver from affected VPCs.

Carla (SRE): dig output snippet:
```
$ dig +short private-api.internal.us-west3.example
10.10.40.12
; TCP connection timed out
```

Mike (NetOps): looks like some traffic is being blackholed at provider nexthops intermittently. I see BFD flaps on transit-1 sessions. BFD counters growing.

Lucas (Infra): can we divert traffic to the redundant transit or failover to other region? Risk: cross-region failover may break low-latency SLAs for some customers.

Raj (Eng-Platform): propose controlled traffic steering to standby transit for affected prefixes while we coordinate with provider. We can update route policies to move 64501 prefixes to alternate path with lower preference.

Carla (SRE): agree. need to coordinate with oncall and change control. We should announce to customers before moving. Tina can do comms.

Tina (Customer Success): ready. Draft message for FinSaaS: "We are investigating intermittent connectivity to PrivateLink endpoints in us-west3. We will apply a temporary route steering to restore connectivity and will follow up with details." Send after mitigation plan is confirmed.

Mike (NetOps): I'm going to test manual policy change on a single PE for a canary. Command snippet:
```
configure router policy
  set preference local-prefer-64501 200
  apply to prefix-list 64501-prefixes on PE-usw3-a
commit
```

Carla (SRE): please run canary on PE-usw3-b instead of a to minimize blast radius. monitor for 5m.

Mike (NetOps): canary started at 3301239950. Redirected 64501-prefixes to transit-2 for PE-usw3-b.

incident-bot: NOTE — Canaries should report back within 5m. If success, escalate to broader steer.

Carla (SRE): watching metrics. TCP resets down by ~70% for the canaried prefixes, latency to private endpoints dropped from 220ms to 38ms.

Tina (Customer Success): telling FinSaaS we have a mitigative change in progress and will escalate if stable.

Lucas (Infra): running a traceroute from FinSaaS tester after canary:
```
traceroute private-api.internal.us-west3.example
 1  10.10.1.1  <1 ms
 2  198.51.100.5  8 ms
 3  203.0.113.9  38 ms
```

Carla (SRE): good signs. but BFD counters still tick on a subset of sessions. provider liaison engaged. I opened ticket with provider support (ticket# PRV-88123) and posted details.

Mike (NetOps): after 10m canary, no regressions. I'm going to roll policy to all PE-usw3 instances at 3301240700 with 30s stagger.

deploy-bot: AUDIT — policy-change by Mike applied to 6 PEs at 3301240700.

Carla (SRE): monitoring post-roll. initial indicators show stable BGP, CPU and packet loss improved. private DNS forwarding successful for FinSaaS and 3 other impacted customers.

Tina (Customer Success): sending update to impacted customers now: stable but still validating. asking customers to report any residual errors.

Raj (Eng-Platform): we should also enable temporary extra TTL on internal DNS responses to reduce lookup load while provider investigates flaps. Any objections?

Carla (SRE): fine with TTL bump for 10m. I'll apply it to the resolver pool for us-west3 at 3301241100.

Mike (NetOps): provider replied: "We observed link-level errors causing BFD timeouts, working on optical layer repair. Suggested mitigation: prefer alternate transit until fiber repaired." ETA from provider is 45-90m.

Carla (SRE): note for postmortem: correlate BFD timer settings vs our expected thresholds; evaluate whether auto-failover thresholds too sensitive for transient fiber errors.

Lucas (Infra): continuing to watch for collateral impact to cross-region replication. so far no issues.

Tina (Customer Success): FinSaaS acknowledges improvement; wants root-cause update once provider fixes fiber. Will keep them informed.

Carla (SRE): marking incident as mitigated for customer impact at 3301241800. Will keep the incident channel open for final provider confirmation and RCA.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — Mitigation in place, customer impact reduced. Maintaining monitoring and awaiting provider repair.

Mike (NetOps): provider updated: repair crew on site, optics replaced at the POP. monitoring shows BFD stable for 15m.

Carla (SRE): good. planning post-incident action items: 1) adjust BFD thresholds for wide-area transits (Raj/Mike), 2) add automatic transient-failure dampening to avoid immediate route steering (Carla/Raj), 3) update runbook to include canary steering steps and comm templates (Tina).

Tina (Customer Success): I'll schedule customer follow-up and send the RCA draft once we have provider confirmation.

Carla (SRE): last check at 3301242300 shows all affected prefixes stable, no withdrawn routes, DNS resolution normal. Closing active mitigation. Keeping channel open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
